title: Plant Growth and Development
seo_title: Plant Growth and Development Class 11 Biology Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 13)
standard_code: Class 11 Biology, Chapter 13: Plant Growth and Development
standard_text: Seed germination; phases of plant growth and plant growth rate; conditions of growth; differentiation, dedifferentiation and redifferentiation; sequence of developmental processes in a plant cell; plant growth regulators – auxin, gibberellin, cytokinin, ethylene, ABA.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 11 Biology worksheets for NCERT Chapter 13 Plant Growth and Development: growth phases and curves, differentiation, the five plant hormones and their uses, photoperiodism and vernalisation. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Five plant growth regulators: auxin, gibberellin, cytokinin, ethylene, ABA.
body_html:
How to think about it

Plant growth is indeterminate and happens at meristems. Growth may be arithmetic or geometric and usually follows an S-shaped (sigmoid) curve with lag, log and stationary phases. Cells differentiate, can dedifferentiate to divide again, and then redifferentiate.

Growth regulators control development: auxins (apical dominance, rooting), gibberellins (stem elongation, bolting), cytokinins (cell division, delaying senescence), ethylene (ripening) and abscisic acid (dormancy, closing stomata). Photoperiodism and vernalisation control flowering.

Example

Hormone for fruit ripening?

a gas

Answer: ethylene

Example

Cabbage bolting?

stem elongation

Answer: gibberellin

Common mistakes

  • Calling ABA a growth promoter.
  • Saying photoperiod is sensed by the flower.
  • Mixing up auxin and cytokinin.
